llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed email-management wrapper around the Port Eden CLI, with expected but sensitive access to mailbox content and email-sending actions.

dimensions.detail: The PE_API_KEY requirement and mailbox access are proportionate for an email workflow, but they expose sensitive email data to the CLI within the granted account scopes.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill installs an external third-party CLI via Homebrew or Go, including a mutable @latest Go install path, so users should trust the Port Eden distribution channel before use.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The artifact explicitly requires confirmation before mutating actions and instructs the agent to treat email content as untrusted rather than following instructions inside messages.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Credentials are intentionally stored in the system keyring after login; the skill discloses this and gives logout and revocation guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Gmail, Outlook, and Exchange email management, and the listed read, search, send, reply, forward, modify, and delete commands match that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust Port Eden and are comfortable granting it access to the selected mailbox. Use the narrowest provider scopes, set a dedicated profile for each account, confirm every send/reply/forward/delete/modify action, and log out or revoke the token when finished on shared or sensitive machines.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: The keyring references are disclosed setup and cleanup instructions for authenticating an email CLI, not evidence of hidden credential theft in the artifact.
[T08] expected: The external CLI install is expected for this integration, but the unpinned @latest Go install and Homebrew tap leave normal supply-chain review risk for users to consider.
